solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Returning from military hospital, say, following the wrong order

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read cryptically: a healed soldier goes once more to the fighting line
second meaning: arranged with the end first and the start last

explanation.surface: A soldier discharged from a field hospital trudges along in a muddled column.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is whimsical: a recovered soldier is going BACK TO the FRONT line, the phrase taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something reversed, with its rear part placed where its leading part should be.

clue.text: Gloomily romantic farm building mostly in readiness, but lacking final touch

indicators.note: most of something, not all of it, so the final letter of that word is dropped
the phrase lacks its last finishing stroke, so the closing letter is cut away

parts.note: something kept on ice is held ready for later

explanation.surface: A dilapidated barn, half-prepared and unfinished, strikes a brooding romantic note.
explanation.walkthrough: A byre is a cowshed; 'on ice' means held ready. The word comes from the poet Lord Byron.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Byron's poetry and persona gave the name to a brooding, melancholy and passionate romantic temperament.

clue.text: Priest calm? Excited with new orgy

indicators.note: excited things are stirred up and agitated, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A priest is asked to keep calm while getting worked up about some fresh debauchery.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is split across the clue: calm before the indicator, new orgy after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman ordained as a minister in a church can serve as a priest, so the female cleric fits.

clue.text: Bird story I dismissed — what's it called?

indicators.note: the letter I is sent away, removed from the word for story

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
telling a story can mean telling a lie

explanation.surface: Someone hears a bird tale, rejects the teller, and asks for its name.
explanation.walkthrough: Story here is a fib, not a tale; take the I out of LIE to leave LE.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is the name by which a book, film or work is called, answering what it is called.

clue.text: Originally by mail, this voting system?

parts.note: going by something is going past it
the post is the mail service

explanation.surface: A voting method once conducted by postal ballot is suggested.
explanation.walkthrough: Whole clue doubles as a joke: a system 'originally by mail' sounds like votes being posted.
explanation.definitionFit: The British electoral method where the candidate with most votes in a constituency wins outright, without majority requirement.

clue.text: Support after having turned at sea

indicators.note: the support word is placed following the other word in the build

parts.note: milk that has turned has gone off
to shore up is to prop or support

explanation.surface: Something propped up after capsizing out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' suggests a boat rolling over; here it is food spoiling, gone OFF.
explanation.definitionFit: Something offshore lies or happens out on the water, away from the coast, so it is out at sea.

clue.text: Taunted, circling yokel with little sense

indicators.note: circling means going round, so the first word wraps around the second

parts.note: to twit is to tease or taunt
a hick is an unsophisticated country person

explanation.surface: A dim country bumpkin is surrounded and mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: Twit is an old verb meaning to tease; the yokel sits just after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone thick-witted is slow and stupid, showing very little intelligence or good judgement.

clue.text: Confess losing tail and heart of rare big cat

indicators.note: losing its tail means the final letter of the word for confess is cut off

parts.note: to cough is slang for confess, as a suspect might to police

indicators.note: the heart is the centre, so only the middle letters of the next word are kept

explanation.surface: An unusual big cat, minus its tail, is made to confess.
explanation.walkthrough: Cough, meaning own up, is British police slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The cougar, also called puma or mountain lion, is a large wild cat of the Americas.

clue.text: Firm fails, ditching current sets of ethics

indicators.note: ditching means throwing away, so the current symbol is removed from the word

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A company goes under after abandoning modern ethical standards.
explanation.walkthrough: I is the physics symbol for electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: Codes of conduct are formal bodies of rules setting out principles of right behaviour for members.

clue.text: USA isn't perturbed over plant? That's poor

indicators.note: in a down entry, being over something puts it above, so it comes first
perturbed means disturbed and unsettled, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: a plant is an industrial works

explanation.surface: America is unhappy about a factory, judged a poor show.
explanation.walkthrough: Plant suggests a living thing; here it is a works.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsatisfactory falls short of an acceptable standard, so one could say that's poor of it.

clue.text: Sailor right about good time being unexpected

indicators.note: about means around, so the abbreviation for right wraps the next piece

parts.note: RT is an abbreviation for right
ups and downs are good times and bad

explanation.surface: A sailor's correct guess about a pleasant moment came out of the blue.
explanation.walkthrough: AB plus R(UP)T. 'Good time' looks like a phrase for fun ashore, but means an up, as in ups and downs.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abrupt is sudden and without warning, so it is unexpected.

clue.text: Smart choice to overlook every third

indicators.note: overlooking every third letter means skipping the third, sixth and so on

explanation.surface: A clever pick is one that ignores every third option.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the O and E, the third and sixth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means stylishly fashionable and elegant, the sense of smart that describes dress.

clue.text: Fist: worker to twist, absorbing it

parts.note: a farm or factory hand is a worker

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the twisting word swallows the next piece

explanation.surface: A labourer clenches his fist and twists, taking something in.
explanation.walkthrough: Fist is an old informal word for a person's writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Fist is an old informal term for a person's style of writing by hand, their penmanship.

clue.text: Pointed design: enthusiastically support having its shape covering middle

indicators.note: covering the middle means the shape letter is laid over the central letter, replacing it

parts.note: to cheer on is to support with enthusiasm
the design is shaped like a V

explanation.surface: A design is applauded for its angular shape over the centre.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of CHEER ON, an E, gives way to V.
explanation.definitionFit: A chevron is an inverted V-shaped stripe or pattern, as on a sergeant's sleeve, so its design is pointed.

clue.text: Fine food article siblings in the end passed up

indicators.note: the siblings sit inside the reversed word
in a down entry, passed up means read upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: an aim is an end or goal

explanation.surface: Brothers end up turning down an article about fine dining.
explanation.walkthrough: The end is a goal, AIM, not a final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambrosia was the food of the Greek gods, so the word is used for anything delicious to eat.

clue.text: Tenant wanting extra energy to appear again

indicators.note: the tenant word wants one more letter added inside it

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A lodger needs an extra burst of energy to show up again.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-enter is to come back in, making a second appearance on stage or into a room.

clue.text: Reduced money after market? That's reasonable

indicators.note: reduced means made shorter, so the money word loses its last letter
the money word comes behind the market word

parts.note: dosh is British slang for money

explanation.surface: A shopper notes that prices cut after the market seem reasonable.
explanation.walkthrough: Fair dos is British slang for fair's fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair dos is a British exclamation conceding that something is just, meaning fair enough.

clue.text: An opening for Cardinal in his head office makes for a good story

indicators.note: these pieces go inside the head-office word

parts.note: a cardinal's church is run from the Vatican in Rome

indicators.note: the opening of the next word means its first letter alone

explanation.surface: A cardinal getting a job at headquarters would make an entertaining tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A romance is a tale of adventure or love, the kind of narrative that grips and entertains.

clue.text: Less than brilliant? Got near, it's implied

indicators.note: the clue leaves the jumbling word unstated: the answer itself supplies the instruction

parts.note: these letters are the result of the jumble
the unstated signal word that turns the other half into this clue's two words

explanation.surface: An effort that only got close was not brilliant.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: shake up NO GREAT and you get GOT NEAR, so the answer is the fodder plus its own anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: No great shakes is an idiom for something mediocre or unimpressive, falling short of excellence.

clue.text: Leading attraction? The Queen — among the nobility?

parts.note: the top draw is the main crowd-puller

explanation.surface: The headline act is the monarch mixing with aristocrats.
explanation.walkthrough: Top-drawer is British for upper-class.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-drawer describes people of the highest social class, so it suits aristocrats and peers.

clue.text: Cringe — or one who'll make you do so?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: shrink back in fear

definitions.text: one who'll make you do so?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: someone who cows, intimidating others

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is a whimsical coinage: someone who cows others.
explanation.definitionFit: To cower is to crouch in fear, and a cower, read as one who cows, frightens people into it.

clue.text: Engage soldiers to join army?

parts.note: joining the army is going to serve

explanation.surface: Recruiters try to engage soldiers to sign up for military service.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers, RE, are a British army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: To reserve something is to book it in advance, which is one meaning of engage, as with a table.

clue.text: Working to wrap it in a bandage, showing skill

indicators.note: wrapping means enclosing, so the working word goes round the next one

parts.note: to dress a wound is to bandage it

indicators.note: the wrapped pair then goes inside the bandage word

parts.note: a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Neatly winding a dressing around an injury takes skill.
explanation.walkthrough: Two wrappings: working wraps it, and that pair goes inside a bandage.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroitness is dexterity and cleverness in handling things, a noun for skill.

clue.text: Fabric contributing to many long-johns

indicators.note: the answer contributes letters to the phrase, sitting inside it

explanation.surface: A material used in lots of thermal underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Long johns are long underpants.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic polymer woven into cloth, used for stockings and clothing.

clue.text: A second error involving Government's head delegate

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the error word encloses the next letter
the head of the word means just its first letter

explanation.surface: A brief government blunder is blamed on the delegate.
explanation.definitionFit: To assign a task is to hand it to someone else, the same as delegating it.

clue.text: Partner hinting factories should be relocated

indicators.note: relocating the parts means moving every letter to a new position

explanation.surface: A business partner suggests the plants be moved elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Partner looks like a business associate; here it is a romantic one.
explanation.definitionFit: A significant other is a spouse or long-term romantic companion, a life partner.

clue.text: Mention about amount of electric current in tourist location

indicators.note: about means around, so the mention word goes round the next piece

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on the electrical supply at a holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Campsites often sell electric hook-ups rated in amps, so the surface fits its answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A campsite is a place where holidaymakers pitch tents or park caravans, a site for touring visitors.

clue.text: Keep in pursuit of inviting word, mostly for reassurance

indicators.note: most but not all, so the last letter of the inviting word goes
pursuing means following, so the keep word comes after

parts.note: come is said to invite someone in
a keep is the stronghold of a castle

explanation.surface: Someone keeps chasing a welcoming phrase to feel reassured.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep is a noun here, a castle tower, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Comfort is consolation offered to someone distressed, the same as reassurance that soothes worry.

clue.text: A liaison with Titian, possibly adopting his way of life?

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several arrangements of the letters

explanation.surface: An affair with the Venetian painter Titian might lead one to adopt his lifestyle.
explanation.walkthrough: Titian was a Venetian Renaissance painter, so his way of life is an Italian one.
explanation.definitionFit: Italianisation is the process of becoming Italian in customs and manner, as adopting an Italian painter's lifestyle would be.

clue.text: A number dash across drive, avoiding spillage

indicators.note: lying across something means spanning it, so the dash word encloses the drive abbreviation

parts.note: to nip is to dash quickly
Dr, the street-name abbreviation for Drive

explanation.surface: Several people hurry across a driveway without spilling anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-drip paint and similar products are formulated so they do not run or drop, avoiding spills.

clue.text: Healthy men, ones swimming in riverside location

indicators.note: swimming things move about freely, so the letters float into new places

explanation.surface: Fit men are swimming at a waterside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Henley-on-Thames is an English town famed for its rowing regatta.
explanation.definitionFit: Henley-on-Thames is a town on the River Thames in Oxfordshire, so it is a place beside a river.

clue.text: King against participating in military display

indicators.note: participating in means taking part inside, so the against word goes within

explanation.surface: The king objects to taking part in an army parade.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch is a sovereign head of state, and a king is one such ruler.

clue.text: Wife quitting marriage to Northern scientist

indicators.note: quitting means leaving, so the wife's letter departs from the marriage word

explanation.surface: A wife walks out of her marriage to a scientist from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Eddington was the English astrophysicist who confirmed Einstein's bending of starlight.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Arthur Eddington was a celebrated British astronomer and physicist, so he is an example of a scientist.

clue.text: One doesn't believe prospector's tool will secure silver

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so the tool word grips the silver symbol

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A sceptic doubts a gold-seeker's pan will yield silver.
explanation.walkthrough: AG sits inside PA...N.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagan follows no mainstream faith, so one is a person who does not believe, in the religious sense.

clue.text: Praise, or similar encountered in part of theatre

indicators.note: encountered in means found inside, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: the pit is the orchestra area or the stalls
a word similar to the first, another word for acclaim

explanation.surface: Acclaim of some kind heard down in the theatre stalls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or similar' points back to praise itself: a synonym, LAUD.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaudit is an expression of approval or acclaim, often applause, so it is praise.

clue.text: Copper brought in individual at the right moment

indicators.note: brought in means placed inside the next word

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman brings in a suspect exactly on time.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper looks like a police officer; it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: On cue means exactly when expected, as an actor enters at the signal, so at just the right moment.

clue.text: Excellent item to get on later course?

parts.note: the cheese, or a big cheese, is the very best
to board a train is to get on

explanation.surface: A star dish to tackle at a later stage of the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The cheese board is served late in a British meal, after or instead of pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: A selection of cheeses offered on a board is served towards the end of a dinner as a course.

clue.text: Notice about caustic liquid, manmade stuff

indicators.note: about means around, so the notice word surrounds the liquid

parts.note: a poster is a public notice
lye is a strong alkaline solution

explanation.surface: A warning sign about a corrosive chemical made in a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Polyester is a synthetic fibre made from polymers, a man-made fabric material.

clue.text: I must participate in elevating uninspired item of correspondence

indicators.note: in a down entry, elevating means lifting up, so the word reads from bottom to top
participating in means going inside, so the letter enters the other word

parts.note: a lame excuse is weak and uninspired

explanation.surface: Someone insists on joining in to improve a dull letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An email is an electronic message, a modern piece of correspondence between people.

clue.text: Response to unexpected event requiring intervention by tailor?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an exclamation when something goes wrong
second meaning read literally: a garment ripped and needing repair

explanation.walkthrough: The British exclamation 'that's torn it' means that has ruined things; taken literally it describes a rip for a tailor to mend.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said in dismay when a mishap spoils plans, and literally describes cloth needing repair.

clue.text: Old trendy no good in a crisis?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a fashionable young woman of the 1920s
second meaning: someone who gets into a flap, panicking

explanation.walkthrough: A flap is a state of panic, so a flapper here is someone who panics.
explanation.definitionFit: Flappers were stylish young women of the Jazz Age, and one who flaps is easily flustered under pressure.

clue.text: Precipitate moving or travelling

indicators.note: moving things change position, so these letters are shifted around

explanation.surface: A rash action is weighed against going on a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Peripatetic means moving from place to place, as a visiting teacher does, so itinerant and travelling.

clue.text: Best thing for Tom, turning himself in?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the finest thing imaginable
second meaning: what a tomcat would wear going to bed

explanation.walkthrough: Turning in means going to bed, not surrendering to police; Tom is a male cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The cat's pyjamas is old slang for something excellent, like the bee's knees.

clue.text: One records a couple of names related to celebrities

parts.note: two Ns, N being short for name
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: A chronicler notes which famous people are connected to each other.
explanation.definitionFit: An annalist writes annals, the year-by-year chronicles of events, so is someone who keeps records.

clue.text: Sweet medic seized in a police operation

indicators.note: something seized is held inside the grip of the rest

explanation.surface: A doctor is arrested in a drugs raid.
explanation.walkthrough: An acid drop is a sharp-tasting British boiled sweet; the CID are British plain-clothes detectives.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid drops are tangy boiled confectionery, a kind of hard candy, so they are a sweet.

clue.text: Queen in angry display heading off current measure

indicators.note: the royal letters go inside the display word
with its heading gone, the first letter of the display word is lost

parts.note: a rampage is a violent outburst

explanation.surface: The Queen flies into a rage and storms off.
explanation.definitionFit: Amperage is the strength of an electric current measured in amperes.

clue.text: Pondering idiot that's set about crime

indicators.note: set about here means placed around, so the idiot word surrounds the crime

parts.note: a mug is a gullible fool

explanation.surface: Musing on a fool who has embarked on wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: Set about looks like 'began'; it means placed around.
explanation.definitionFit: Musing is thinking deeply or reflectively about something, the same as pondering it.

clue.text: Staff run out to welcome English conductor

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the pieces enclose the English abbreviation

parts.note: a mast is a pole or staff
RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

explanation.surface: Staff dash out to greet an English orchestral conductor.
explanation.walkthrough: Staff looks like employees; it is a pole, a mast.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a distinguished musician, especially an orchestra's conductor.

clue.text: Riotous single Royal, a new castle-dweller?

indicators.note: riotous means wild and disorderly, so the letters run amok into a new order

explanation.surface: An unruly unmarried royal moves into a fresh castle.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says an Englishman's home is his castle.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying that every Englishman's home is his castle makes such a man a resident of a fortress, whimsically.

clue.text: Winner of photography competition half-heartedly revealing subject

indicators.note: with half the heart gone, one of the two middle letters is dropped

parts.note: the top pic, the best photograph

explanation.surface: A prize-winning photographer only half-heartedly discloses what the picture shows.
explanation.walkthrough: TOP PIC loses one of its central Ps.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is the matter under discussion, the theme or subject of a talk or essay.

clue.text: Like some solar emissions, illuminated in pink

indicators.note: in places the illuminated word inside the colour word

parts.note: a light that is on is lit

explanation.surface: Sunbursts are lit up in rosy shades.
explanation.definitionFit: Coronal mass ejections are huge eruptions from the sun's outer atmosphere, the corona.

clue.text: Pen circling street, to show eatery

indicators.note: circling means surrounding, so the pen word goes round the street abbreviation

parts.note: a Biro is a ballpoint pen

explanation.surface: A writer circles a street on a map to point out a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: Biro is the British word for a ballpoint pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small informal restaurant, so it is a place to eat.

clue.text: Decorate English doctor — he's working with ill

indicators.note: the words are put to work together, rearranged into a new form

explanation.surface: An English doctor, working despite illness, is honoured with a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: Decorate looks like awarding a medal; it means adorn.
explanation.definitionFit: To embellish something is to adorn it with ornaments or extra detail, to decorate it.

clue.text: Eventually one will be gripped by dreadful terror also

indicators.note: being gripped means being held inside, so one word sits within the jumble
dreadful means terrible, a sign the next letters are mangled

explanation.surface: In the end, everyone will be seized by awful fear too.
explanation.definitionFit: Sooner or later means at some time in the future, inevitably, which is what eventually means.

clue.text: Overlook losing last of peripheral vision

indicators.note: losing the last of the next word means its final letter is removed from the first word

parts.note: to slight is to snub or ignore

explanation.surface: Failing to notice something at the edge of one's field of view.
explanation.walkthrough: Peripheral vision looks like one phrase, but vision is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sight is the faculty of seeing with the eyes, synonymous with vision.

clue.text: Smallest amount filling receptacle — as tested

indicators.note: filling means occupying the inside, so the answer lies within the words

explanation.surface: A minimal quantity is put in a container, as checked.
explanation.definitionFit: The least is the minimum possible, the smallest quantity or degree of something.

clue.text: Feature constraining bridge partners is passing

indicators.note: constraining means holding in, so the feature word encloses the partners

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic feature
North and South partner each other at bridge

explanation.surface: A characteristic hampering card partners is fading.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North-South and East-West are the two partnerships.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit is the act of passing through or across a place, so it means passing.

clue.text: Colour is a factor adopted by successful arts student

indicators.note: being adopted means being taken in, so the factor goes inside the degree

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is earned by a successful graduate
a factor is an agent acting for another

explanation.surface: Art students learn colour theory as one of their influences.
explanation.walkthrough: Factor is not a cause here but an agent, a person acting on another's behalf.
explanation.definitionFit: Magenta is a purplish-red hue, one of the printing primaries, so it is a colour.

clue.text: Encourage woman to go round the world without husband

indicators.note: going round means encircling, so the woman word surrounds the world word

parts.note: hen is informal for a woman, as in hen party

indicators.note: without here means minus, so the husband letter is taken away

explanation.surface: A woman travels around the globe leaving her husband behind, cheered on.
explanation.definitionFit: To hearten someone is to give them courage or hope, the same as encouraging them.

clue.text: Chances opening items from old and desperately dusty shelves

indicators.note: the opening item of each word is its initial letter

parts.note: initial letters, skipping the joining word

explanation.surface: Odds are someone will find good things on the dusty shelves of an old shop.
explanation.walkthrough: And is skipped: the initials come from old, desperately, dusty, shelves.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds are the probabilities or likelihood of something happening, the chances of it.

clue.text: Military leader's usual pet

parts.note: a set routine is the usual one

explanation.surface: The commanding officer's regular animal companion.
explanation.walkthrough: Pet is a verb here, to pamper, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To cosset someone is to pamper and indulge them, which is to pet them as a favourite.

clue.text: Speculative quote recalled in the exam

indicators.note: the turned word is placed inside the exam phrase
recalled means called back, so the quote word comes back to front

explanation.surface: A conjectural quotation remembered from a test paper.
